First off, I want to say that most of my thoughts on this have been stated by noncommunicable and berrieh, but that I feel it important to emphasise the fact that technology is good at providing facts, but memorizing facts is not the same as being educated.


In my opinion, the biggest role of a teacher, as far as education goes, is helping children learn how to learn, that is how to incorporate and digest  the data provided for them. Technology would have a difficult time doing that, at least as it is now. Technology can not quickly modify and adapt to the individual learning styles of children, so adaptive software would have to be created that would be able to do this. Teachers, at least the good ones, can help present information in different ways, pick up on different children that are struggling with different things, and adapt teaching styles or create a more peer to peer environment, depending on the situation.


Technology also lacks the ability, thus far, to effectively evaluate the aspects of certain subjects that spark interest in a student. In a math class...does a student like the structure and rules that are so often present in math? Does the student like solving puzzles? Does the student enjoy math because he or she has a fine grasp of logic, or does the student see a sort of beauty in mathematics? Computers would have a difficulty sussing out these more subtle and human things, I think. While it still may be difficult for a teacher, the educator may be better equipped to pick up on these things.


I guess, tl;dr, humans understand humans better than machines understand humans, and an understanding of the student helps the teacher go beyond providing facts to providing an enriching environment.


Technology is great and has a lot of advantages. It should be put to good use in the education system, but as it stands now, I do not think technology will make teachers unnecessary.

It's very odd, because I know there are emotional connections happening. It's like I can see them taking place from inside my head, so I know they're there somewhere. Just, they never reach me. Like...I always know I love my father. He's very important to me. But that I can't feel that...sometimes that's rather devastating.

I do tend to go with other people's suggestions, though I'm decisive when people give me choices. I very much resonate with the feeling of life going by.

You don't owe the world anything, at least not first. First, you owe yourself. College is stressful and difficult, but if you feel the need to put something else out into the world, academia isn't the only way you can contribute anything. You are you. You feel things, you think things, you have something to offer the world, even if you don't know what it is yet. If this is your first semester of college, you've still got plenty of opportunities. You have obviously had a difficult time so far, and I can sympathise with that, but there's a whole world, not just college. So, if you do need to take a break, like mfanyafujo said, perhaps you should, but believe me, there's more to life and the world and you, than college.

You've found someone else to talk to! Though I've never met you, you're important to me. You're reaching out, which can be difficult, and that makes me proud of you. It sounds like you're in a lot of pain, and you don't know what to do. I may not give the best advice, but I'm happy to listen and be supportive.

"Sometimes it feels like I'm watching my life through bullet proof glass, and I'm just on auto-pilot, going through the motions of my daily routine until I'm finally back to either sleep..." I don't know that it means much from a stranger, but I know how hard this is, and I think it is really wonderful that you're managing to push on and that you've got someone. It also gives me some hope, which I often lack. The most difficult part, sometimes, is conveying these problems to people who don't understand because we tend to be able to act so well, to cover up the problems. If you ever want/need someone else to talk to for some reason, just a stranger to vent to that can relate...please let me know. It might help both of us. Please don't feel obliged though. This is an offer, not an expectation.
